approach.method_basis: The Parent is an ant colony optimizer that builds each molecular graph from an empty state. At each step it chooses a starting atom, attaches an atom to an existing site, closes a ring bond, or stops. Fixed aggregate frequencies from an unlabeled molecular corpus supply chemical preferences, including attachment, ring-closure and stopping weights. A separate table of task-local pheromones multiplies those preferences. The Parent identifies a reusable attachment component by the central atom's identity, charge, explicit hydrogens, degree, used bond order and ring membership, together with the proposed bond and new atom. Ring-closure components use both endpoint descriptions and their path length. Initial reinforcement comes from an exact reconstruction of the best supported starting observation. After feedback, all pheromones evaporate and only the highest-scoring accepted molecule in that batch deposits credit on its actual construction trace, once per distinct key. Positive lower and upper bounds preserve exploration. Later ants share the credited local components even when they occur inside different partial molecules.
approach.novelty: I add neighborhood-resolved pheromone credit: an attachment site also carries a sorted description of its directly bonded neighbors, and a ring closure carries this description at both endpoints. A move that was rewarded beside one arrangement of atoms and bonds will therefore share that reward only with the same bounded neighborhood. For example, the same central carbon description can acquire different credit when its neighboring atom is oxygen instead of carbon. This tests the Parent's observed loss of selectivity, where almost every accepted ant reused reinforcement but very few improved the incumbent. The lineage currently contains only the original ant colony root, so no sibling has tested a finer pheromone key. The corpus-derived heuristic still uses its original contexts; the new distinction acts specifically through which construction decisions share accepted winner credit.

hypothesis: Refine only the Parent's attachment and ring-closure pheromone keys with fixed, permutation-invariant one-bond neighborhood descriptors so accepted winner reinforcement transfers between matching local neighborhoods instead of all sites sharing the Parent's coarser endpoint description.

finding_summary.headline: Neighborhood credit localized and lifted the screening mean, but successful molecules remained rare
finding_summary.insights: This experiment separates local credit discrimination from productive molecular search. Different neighborhoods really were being collapsed by the old keys, and the new keys distinguish them without changing the legal chemistry or fixed heuristic weights. Matching neighborhoods also recur often enough to transfer credit across different partial molecules, so the refinement did not eliminate transfer through excessive sparsity. Yet most ants still inherit some online credit, and only 5.84% of the observed split-menu groups carried unequal refined pheromones. More precise keys therefore changed specific decisions without making successful whole molecules common. The chemistry explains why the modest mean gain should not be read as a broadly improved generator. The molecular assessment found a compact acyclic urea behind the strongest score increase, but long unsaturated chains and unconventional ring assemblies still dominate. Mean atom count fell slightly, while ring-closure actions fell sharply and terminations at the 64-atom ceiling became more frequent. In every task the late molecules were larger than the early molecules. Local credit refinement alone did not produce sustained access to compact, organized, functionalized chemistry. The result supports the implementation and shows a descriptive gain on this seed; it does not establish a reliable oracle-score benefit of selective credit. Larger changes in different objectives nearly cancel, some counted gains are near numerical ties, and the same-menu probability comparisons do not score unsubmitted alternatives. Whether broader molecular constraints or a better size and termination prior can make the now-demonstrated local discrimination useful remains open, as does its reliability across seeds.
finding_summary.results: The intended credit localization happened. Across the five task-specific tables, 3,027 attachment keys and 6,522 ring-closure keys separated previously shared neighborhoods. All 145 online winner updates withheld deposits from other neighborhoods when opportunities existed, totaling 75,964 alternative/update pairs. Every one of 10,719 mixed-neighborhood update probes increased the winner neighborhoods' conditional probability mass. Later construction contained 18,485 selected moves whose conditional probabilities changed and whose exact neighborhoods traced to earlier accepted online winners. The optimization gain was much smaller than the amount of activity. Among accepted ants that reused online credit, 7 of 1,396 beat their pre-batch incumbent, compared with 3 of 1,399 for the Parent; reuse still reached about 96% of accepted ants. All strict incumbent beaters increased from 8 to 12, but three of the new online-reusing docking beaters were steps of at most 0.00000044 along a low score plateau. The single screening seed's mean final Top-1 rose from 0.2523 to 0.2579. The sitagliptin multi-property score rose from 0.0980 to 0.2392, while dopamine-receptor docking fell from 0.1371 to 0.0289 and decoration hopping fell from 0.5534 to 0.5484. The zaleplon and median-molecule scores stayed at 0.3051 and 0.1678. No generated molecule beat the supplied starting incumbent on three of the five objectives. All 1,450 submitted molecules were accepted; one additional local construction repeated a molecule and was replaced before submission.

molecular.headline: Long polyene chains dominate; occasional polar cages and a compact urea score better, but conventional scaffold chemistry remains sparse.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied task trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read for seed 0. Each contains 290 optimizer proposals plus 10 initial observations. The generated population consists mainly of long, repeatedly unsaturated carbon chains, interrupted by amines, enamines, occasional imines, ethers and carbonyls. Rings are substantial in amount but often unconventional in arrangement: partially unsaturated carbocycles and dense fused or bridged assemblies occur alongside isolated aryl segments. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.3966 to 0.8966, while aromatic-text rates range from 0.1241 to 0.5690; these are fractions of strings carrying a feature, not aromatic atom fractions or assessments of ring quality. Mean SMILES lengths range from 60.1 to 76.5. Direct atom counts from the trajectories show that shorter strings than the Parent frequently reflect fewer closures and branches rather than a substantial size reduction. The emitted structures have no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry, and inspection also found no specified alkene geometry. All supplied generated SMILES parsed with RDKit, which establishes readable molecular graphs, not stability or synthetic accessibility. The quality labels describe substantial ring occurrence, sparse aromatic organization, questionable preparative chemistry, weak resemblance to ordinary medicinal chemistry and recurrent polyene motifs despite distinct molecular identities. Atom and functional-group counts below are direct structural readings of the supplied SMILES; all scores are the recorded evaluator values. Digest medians displayed as 0.0 are rounded and must not be interpreted as a majority of exactly zero observations.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 73.6; direct heavy-atom counts average 47.46 and reach 64. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.8966 and 0.5690. Much of this ring content is a carbocycle or aryl segment embedded in a long polyene, rather than a compact aromatic scaffold. Evaluation 11, the best generated structure, is a compact, densely bridged nitrogen-containing polycycle bearing a nitrile, chlorine and cyclic ketones. Other higher examples include a partially unsaturated N/O polycycle and a nitrogen-free aryl-containing enone/aldehyde chain. Late structures are predominantly long hydrocarbon-rich polyenes, sometimes with ketones, aldehydes or a nitrile. Conventional fragments are recognizable, but their extended unsaturation and crowded ring combinations make synthesis and isolation questionable.
liabilities: Long polyenes and conjugated carbonyl chains create numerous unspecified alkene geometries and potential chemical-stability burdens.
Dense bridged rings with extensive unsaturation and unassigned stereochemistry need geometric and synthetic scrutiny; successful SMILES parsing does not resolve those concerns.
missing_features: Repeated production of compact, conventionally substituted aromatic NH heterocycles with an attached amide, as seen in the best supplied initial molecule; generated aromatic content is frequently carried on long unsaturated extensions.

Sustained access to the compact polar arrangements found among the higher generated examples. The final proposals mostly lose their concentrated nitrogen/carbonyl organization; the data do not identify one mandatory heteroatom motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 24-heavy-atom bridged nitrile at evaluation 11 scores 0.19324099086270913; the 21-heavy-atom N/O polycycle at evaluation 65 scores 0.17464941125558517. The nitrogen-free, shorter carbonyl-containing structure at evaluation 176 still scores 0.13915472870419515, so nitrogen alone cannot explain the gradient. Long final polyenes score zero or near zero; evaluation 300 has 64 heavy atoms and score 0.0. Exactly 130 of the 290 generated proposals score zero. The clearest association is with compactness and functional-group arrangement, not simply having a ring: many zero-scoring chains also contain rings. The supplied indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 remains best overall at 0.3051048083696145. Compared with Parent n-3ab6a944e3dd, ring-closure/aromatic-text rates rise from 0.6103/0.2172 to 0.8966/0.5690 and the generated maximum moves from 0.1775836262122333 to 0.19324099086270913, while that initial overall best remains unchanged.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 75.3 and direct heavy-atom count averages 50.05. Ring-closure rate is 0.8345, but aromatic-text rate is only 0.2655. The best generated molecule at evaluation 223 combines aryl-containing fused ring units, amide groups and nitrogen-containing linkers with a very long alkenyl appendage. Evaluation 26 is smaller and contains a fused N/O ring assembly, an amino substituent and an imine/N-N-containing chain. Other proposals distribute amines, enamines, imines, ethers and amides through long unsaturated backbones. The late molecules retain scattered rings and polar groups but look like extended polyene constructs; their synthesis is considerably less straightforward than the supplied conventionally substituted aromatic starting molecules.
liabilities: Extended polyenes with repeated amine/enamine and occasional imine or hydrazone-like functionality impose stability and stereochemical complexity.
Some highly fused N/O assemblies and densely unsaturated ring junctions have questionable preparative accessibility despite acceptable formal valence.
missing_features: Reliable production of clearly substituted aryl and carbonyl-bearing nitrogen heterocycle arrangements like those present in the stronger initial observations; such organization is diluted by unsaturated tails in much of the generated set.

Compact variants that preserve a polar ring system while varying its substituents. The two leading generated examples show that both compact and large structures can reach the upper observed band, but no clean analogue series identifies the decisive arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The generated maximum is 0.5468883205456095 at evaluation 223, versus the observed floor of 0.5 for hydrocarbon-rich chains and sparsely functionalized carbocycles. An aromatic/N/O-rich 29-heavy-atom molecule at evaluation 26 scores 0.5441609421000981, close to the 64-heavy-atom generated maximum. Thus ring-associated polar functionality and aromatic organization distinguish the higher band more consistently than size alone; neither a universal growth benefit nor a universal small-molecule preference follows. The final cited proposals range from 0.500866325911808 to 0.5162088883649651. The best supplied initial molecule scores 0.548381482770623 and remains best overall. The Parent generated maximum was 0.5533540672422114; its ring-closure/aromatic-text rates were 0.9448/0.4241. The current products have less ring and aromatic occurrence while retaining almost the same mean atom count.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 76.5 and direct heavy-atom count averages 51.10. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.5345 and 0.1241. The upper observed score band is dominated by very long, mostly nonaromatic polyenes with chain amines or enamines and occasional partially unsaturated carbocycles or N-containing rings. Acyclic and cyclic structures occur at the identical maximum. Smaller low-scoring examples include propene, aldehyde/imine-containing structures, an acyl chloride and an unusual three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl graph. The extended chains and unusual reactive or constrained outliers support questionable synthetic plausibility; the score plateau is not evidence that these are convincing receptor ligands.
liabilities: Long chains with many unassigned double-bond geometries provide poorly specified three-dimensional structures and substantial hydrophobic bulk.
Low-scoring proposals include an acyl chloride, unusual sulfur bonding and a very small cyclic dicarbonyl; these raise direct reactivity or strain concerns.
missing_features: Compact scaffold coverage comparable to the Parent structures that received scores above the present plateau. The current high band mainly samples long unsaturated chains rather than demonstrating an improved compact binding arrangement.

Conventional aromatic and saturated nitrogen-ring arrangements are underrepresented, not absent. Their independent benefit and any receptor-specific missing pharmacophore cannot be established from these tied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Exactly 111 generated molecules share the maximum 0.02885837683273086. Evaluation 96 has 60 heavy atoms and an N-containing ring, while evaluation 123 is an acyclic 53-heavy-atom amine/polyene at that same score. Propene scores 0.004764078329913475 and the three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl scores 0.003770354034741671. The observed progression toward larger chains ends in a repeated plateau, which cannot distinguish a favored ring system, amine placement or binding geometry. The best initial observation is 0.01904115112334333; another initial molecule already contains an N-methyl saturated amine ring yet scores only 0.0003786988088202195, so simply adding such an amine is unsupported guidance. The Parent had a compact fused, nitrogen-substituted polycyclic outlier at 0.13712669868003655, above this plateau. Its ring-closure/aromatic-text rates were 0.9724/0.2897, versus the current 0.5345/0.1241. Those differences describe a loss of ring-rich output, without establishing why the docking scores differ.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 73.1 and direct heavy-atom count averages 50.47. Ring-closure rate is 0.8552 and aromatic-text rate is 0.4310. The best generated molecule at evaluation 62 is a large, partly aromatic N-rich fused assembly with carbonyl functionality, a fluoro-substituted unsaturated linker, an aryl amine connection, a tertiary amide and an amino-ether tail. Other higher examples are densely bridged nitrogen cages with nitriles and ketones, or complex heteroaromatic/carbonyl-containing systems. The lower band contains acyclic amino-polyenes of both small and very large size. The ring-rich structures have more differentiated functionality, but their congested topology and long tails leave synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: Congested fused and bridged unsaturated rings, together with unspecified stereochemistry, complicate three-dimensional feasibility and route planning.
Long amino-polyene and aldehyde-containing tails add unsaturation and reactive functionality without consistently retaining the organized polar scaffold of the better examples.
missing_features: Routine access to conventionally linked aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl heterocyclic units like those in the stronger supplied starting molecules, without converting the whole structure into a bridged cage or a long polyene.

Controlled substitution around a retained compact ring system, which would help separate the observed contributions of ring identity, carbonyl placement and heteroatom arrangement; the present examples change several of these together.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The generated maximum is 0.12097167578182677 at evaluation 62; the bridged nitrile/ketone cage at evaluation 11 scores 0.1000061734111242. The short amino-polyene at evaluation 32 scores 0.0, and the 64-heavy-atom acyclic nitrogen-containing chain at evaluation 226 scores 0.006228601608634516. Thus the distinction is not simply small versus large: organized rings and associated functionality separate the higher band from chain-only structures. The best supplied initial aromatic, carbonyl-rich heterocycle remains best overall at 0.1678386594791329. The Parent generated maximum was 0.13095077916237702. Aromatic-text occurrence increases from 0.3069 to 0.4310, while ring-closure occurrence falls from 0.9517 to 0.8552 and the overall best remains the same initial molecule. More aromatic text alone therefore does not establish better scaffold organization.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 60.1 and direct heavy-atom count averages 39.66. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.3966 and 0.1379, so most generated structures are acyclic and nonaromatic. The best generated molecule at evaluation 62 is a 19-heavy-atom substituted urea with unsaturated arms ending in an aldehyde and an imine. Other higher examples include a complex N/O fused carbonyl-containing structure, an acyclic imine/vinyl-ether-rich molecule and a short amino-polyenone. Later proposals are predominantly hydrocarbon polyenes with occasional amines or terminal aldehydes. The urea itself is a conventional linkage, but its unsaturated imine/aldehyde substituents and the broader polyene population raise stability and synthesis concerns.
liabilities: The best-scoring molecule still combines multiple unsaturated bonds with terminal imine and aldehyde functionality; its score does not establish stability or a practical route.
The dominant late polyenes have extensive unspecified alkene geometry, low polar-group density and frequent terminal carbonyl reactivity.
missing_features: Consistent regeneration of compact molecules with concentrated carbonyl and nitrogen functionality. The best urea is an isolated example, while late products mostly return to extended unsaturated chains.

Chemically stable variants of the compact polar arrangements already receiving higher scores, with less reliance on imines, enamines and aldehydes. Improved stability is a chemical need here, not an independently demonstrated scoring requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact acyclic urea scores 0.23921423452807236. The N/O fused structure at evaluation 20 scores 0.0814995806289838 and the acyclic heteroatom-rich structure at evaluation 43 scores 0.04838092252183626. The long final aldehyde/polyene at evaluation 299 has 64 heavy atoms and score 0.0; exactly 108 of the 290 optimizer proposals score zero. The higher examples favor compactness and concentrated polar functionality relative to long hydrocarbon-rich chains, but they do not establish that a ring, fluorination or a particular named heterocycle is required: the best example has none of those features. The initial maximum was 0.0020944534688323298. The Parent maximum was 0.09799523162987753 for a cyclic amino-polycarbonyl/lactone structure; the present best instead uses an acyclic urea arrangement. Ring-closure/aromatic-text occurrence falls from the Parent values 0.5483/0.1966 to 0.3966/0.1379. The higher best score therefore does not correspond to more aromatic or cyclic chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean heavy-atom counts from the generated trajectories range from 39.66 to 51.10, against 28.40 for the shared initial set. In each trajectory the final 50 proposals have a higher mean atom count than the first 50. The compact 19-heavy-atom urea at score 0.23921423452807236 and the 24-heavy-atom nitrile cage at 0.19324099086270913 contrast with long final polyenes scoring zero. A different upper-band example has 64 heavy atoms, so the evidence does not justify a universal preference for the smallest possible molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Compact functionalized molecules are reached occasionally but are not sustained as a substantial output regime.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide a corpus-grounded size and termination prior that keeps compact functionalized structures readily reachable while retaining multiple size classes. Measure size with atom counts and unsaturated-chain extent; shorter SMILES alone can reflect lost ring structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest ring-closure rates span 0.3966 to 0.8966, while aromatic-text rates span 0.1241 to 0.5690. The examples include isolated rings embedded in long chains, highly bridged unsaturated cages and an unusual three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl. Direct ring inspection finds only 6 to 10 proposals per 290 with a saturated nitrogen-containing ring, including rings inside cages; this is a deficit of conventional scaffold coverage, not an inability to close any ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring closure is common, but conventional aromatic and saturated heterocyclic organization is poorly represented.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make common aromatic rings, saturated heterocycles and supported fusion patterns reliably available with controlled substitution and attachment geometry. Corpus-derived ring-environment support or coherent ring motifs could supply this capability without identifying the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The generated examples contain amines, enamines, imines, ethers and carbonyls, so heteroatoms are not absent. Higher examples include a compact urea, nitrile/carbonyl ring assemblies and aromatic amide-containing initial molecules, but many later proposals consist mainly of carbon chains with scattered nitrogen or terminal aldehydes. Direct inspection finds only 4 to 10 generated molecules per trajectory carrying an aromatic nitrogen atom.
transferable_gaps.gap: Polar groups are often dispersed through unsaturated chains instead of organized into compact, chemically distinct environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve the bond-order and neighboring-group context that distinguishes an amine, enamine, imine, amide, urea or heteroaromatic nitrogen. Enable compact variants of observed polar arrangements and controlled changes around those arrangements so scalar feedback can compare related chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All supplied optimizer SMILES parse, yet the cited structures include dense unsaturated bridges, a very small cyclic dicarbonyl, acyl chloride functionality and repeated enal/enone or imine-containing chains. Some of these motifs appear in higher-scoring examples, so recorded reward alone does not establish an isolable or readily synthesizable product.
transferable_gaps.gap: Readable valence-consistent graphs still include chemically questionable ring and reactive-group combinations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use corpus support for complete ring/fusion environments and reactive-group co-occurrences when weighting or validating constructions. Track geometric and functional-group compatibility separately from formal valence, while retaining supported polyene and polycyclic chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre rate is 0.0 on every trajectory, and the full generated strings contain no explicit alkene-geometry markers. Long polyenes and multiply bridged ring systems therefore reach evaluation without their potential stereochemical alternatives being explicitly distinguished. These observations establish missing output specification, not that any particular objective necessarily rewards one isomer.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemistry even when its unsaturation and ring topology create isomeric choices.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Allow feasible tetrahedral and alkene stereochemistry to be assigned, retained through canonicalization and explored as part of molecular identity. Constrain assignments using the actual ring geometry and local bonding rather than an objective-specific stereochemical template.

method_name: MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar
method_thesis: Anchor the method in MAX-MIN Ant System: construct solutions probabilistically from components, evaporate their pheromone weights, reinforce the iteration-best solution, and bound every pheromone weight away from zero and excessive dominance. [Stutzle and Hoos, Sections 2 and 4](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~hoos/Publ/fgcs00.pdf) describe this mechanism. Our molecular adaptation constructs a fresh graph from an empty state through valence-aware atom, bond, ring-closure and termination actions. Choice probabilities combine a fixed chemical heuristic with task-local pheromones keyed by the local attachment context and action, allowing a useful action to transfer between different partial graphs. Preparation uses the permitted unlabeled corpus only for aggregate construction frequencies and stopping statistics. Initialize pheromones broadly, reconstruct valid construction traces for the supplied scored molecules, and use their best trace for the initial reinforcement. Generate the announced batch through complete new construction trajectories; only accepted whole-molecule feedback drives evaporation and reinforcement of that batch's best trace. Resample failed or duplicate constructions locally. There is no stored complete-molecule library, corpus ranking or fixed product enumeration. The hypothesis is that reusing successful local construction choices across new molecular combinations raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Whether coarse construction contexts carry useful reward information quickly enough is unproven; pheromone concentration or validity alone is not success.

activation_observables.measurement: The Parent has exactly one live pheromone value for every old ADD/CLOSE key. Independently replay logged initial and generated action traces, regenerate N at each pre-action graph, and join each registered refined key to its exact old-key projection. Count old keys represented by at least two distinct neighborhood descriptors in actual construction menus, their refined-child counts, and their coverage among selected nontrivial actions. Require at least one observed ADD/CLOSE split; more table entries caused only by new old keys are not activation. Verify permutation invariance, symmetric CLOSE endpoints, absence of whole-graph/index fields, unchanged START/STOP keys, exact initial/submission identities and identical concrete legal actions and eta values to the Parent's grammar on the same replayed graphs. Report ADD and CLOSE separately and identify unsupported or missing opportunities.
activation_observables.name: old_pheromone_keys_split_by_bonded_neighborhood

activation_observables.measurement: At every initial and online update, independently join the winner to accepted scores and its exact original trace. Project the winner's refined ADD/CLOSE keys to Parent keys, then identify already registered alternative refined keys sharing a rewarded Parent key but absent from the winner trace. Under the Parent's rule these alternatives share the same deposited parameter; under the Child they must receive exactly zero additive deposit while winner refinements receive exactly the inherited rank deposit once each. Count these segregated alternatives and the accepted updates producing them, separately for initial and online credit, and require a nonzero online segregation count. Reconstruct all explicit and implicit evaporation, clipping and source membership, including floor/saturation cases. Probe the stored legal menus after evaporation plus clipping without any deposit and after the actual deposit plus clipping; for mixed winner/nonwinner refinements within an old-key group, report conditional winner-refinement mass shifts and bound-saturated cases. Every non-saturated opportunity with a strictly raised winner weight must increase its conditional mass. Zero additive credit is the claim; normalized probabilities of unreinforced alternatives can also move through normalization.
activation_observables.name: neighborhood_specific_winner_deposit_segregation

activation_observables.measurement: For actual generated branching menus after online feedback, aggregate concrete eta^beta weights by refined key and old-key projection. Within every old ADD/CLOSE group containing multiple refined keys, compare normalized eta^beta*tau^alpha against normalized eta^beta. The Parent's conditional distribution equals the latter exactly because a single shared tau cancels, giving a zero conditional-total-variation reference. Report mean and maximum conditional total variation, the number of groups with unequal refined tau and nonzero variation, and the number of actual selected actions whose conditional probability differs. Require later selected nontrivial actions with nonzero conditional displacement attributable to an earlier online winner, and reconstruct their values from accepted update history. Count exact refined-key reuse from accepted source winners across independently replayed different partial graphs, excluding START/STOP and same-partial-graph repeats; require at least one later accepted molecule with such online reuse. Report cases where a coarser source match exists but a neighborhood match does not. Separate terminal updates without later generation and saturated, single-refinement or unvisited groups. This same-menu comparison establishes contextual probability discrimination, not a counterfactual selected molecule or oracle-score gain.
activation_observables.name: refined_credit_changes_later_within_context_probabilities

activation_observables.measurement: Using only accepted trajectory scores and source-linked original traces, report incumbent-beating counts and fractions among ants reusing earlier online-refined attachment/closure keys, alongside the fraction of all accepted ants that reuse such keys. Compare descriptively with the Parent's three incumbent beaters among 1,399 accepted online-reusing ants, and also report all accepted incumbent beaters, per-batch best scores and initial-to-final incumbent changes so a smaller reuse denominator cannot manufacture an improvement claim. Summarize generated atom counts and termination/closure frequencies as possible mediators or competing explanations, not as extra targeted mechanisms. Final comparative score evidence comes only from protocol-controlled replicas. If the first three observables activate but this yield does not improve, record negative usefulness evidence rather than relabeling correct key refinement as an implementation failure.
activation_observables.name: accepted_improvement_yield_after_selective_credit

applicability_conditions: Applies to the Parent's fresh graph-building ant colony with fixed corpus heuristics, accepted scalar feedback, original generating traces and separate labeled state for each objective.

The supplied evidence contains only the completed screening replica. Parent activation is established there, but attribution of weak optimization to coarse credit remains a hypothesis requiring the bound comparison.

Useful selectivity requires both multiple bonded neighborhoods inside some old context-action keys and repeated matching refined neighborhoods across different partial molecules. Extremely sparse refined keys can remove useful transfer, while universally repeated neighborhoods can leave the original problem unresolved.

This fixed one-bond descriptor distinguishes local surroundings, not complete scaffolds or long-range arrangement. The Parent's weak aromatic organization, large unsaturated products, traversal preferences and unsupported stereochemical cases can continue to limit performance.

The Parent's aggregate grammar and all heuristic eta values remain fixed; this does not test corpus environment support filtering, equivalent-order score augmentation, a learned predictor, a different deposition schedule or a new construction vocabulary.

Within-old-key probability comparisons use the same observed menu and exact arithmetic. They do not assume the Parent would visit the same states or assign oracle scores to alternatives that were never submitted.

approach.method_basis: The Parent is an ant colony optimizer that builds each molecular graph from an empty state. At each step it chooses a starting atom, attaches an atom to an existing site, closes a ring bond, or stops. Fixed aggregate frequencies from an unlabeled molecular corpus supply chemical preferences, including attachment, ring-closure and stopping weights. A separate table of task-local pheromones multiplies those preferences. The Parent identifies a reusable attachment component by the central atom's identity, charge, explicit hydrogens, degree, used bond order and ring membership, together with the proposed bond and new atom. Ring-closure components use both endpoint descriptions and their path length. Initial reinforcement comes from an exact reconstruction of the best supported starting observation. After feedback, all pheromones evaporate and only the highest-scoring accepted molecule in that batch deposits credit on its actual construction trace, once per distinct key. Positive lower and upper bounds preserve exploration. Later ants share the credited local components even when they occur inside different partial molecules.
approach.novelty: I add neighborhood-resolved pheromone credit: an attachment site also carries a sorted description of its directly bonded neighbors, and a ring closure carries this description at both endpoints. A move that was rewarded beside one arrangement of atoms and bonds will therefore share that reward only with the same bounded neighborhood. For example, the same central carbon description can acquire different credit when its neighboring atom is oxygen instead of carbon. This tests the Parent's observed loss of selectivity, where almost every accepted ant reused reinforcement but very few improved the incumbent. The lineage currently contains only the original ant colony root, so no sibling has tested a finer pheromone key. The corpus-derived heuristic still uses its original contexts; the new distinction acts specifically through which construction decisions share accepted winner credit.

finding_summary.headline: Neighborhood credit localized and lifted the screening mean, but successful molecules remained rare
finding_summary.insights: This experiment separates local credit discrimination from productive molecular search. Different neighborhoods really were being collapsed by the old keys, and the new keys distinguish them without changing the legal chemistry or fixed heuristic weights. Matching neighborhoods also recur often enough to transfer credit across different partial molecules, so the refinement did not eliminate transfer through excessive sparsity. Yet most ants still inherit some online credit, and only 5.84% of the observed split-menu groups carried unequal refined pheromones. More precise keys therefore changed specific decisions without making successful whole molecules common. The chemistry explains why the modest mean gain should not be read as a broadly improved generator. The molecular assessment found a compact acyclic urea behind the strongest score increase, but long unsaturated chains and unconventional ring assemblies still dominate. Mean atom count fell slightly, while ring-closure actions fell sharply and terminations at the 64-atom ceiling became more frequent. In every task the late molecules were larger than the early molecules. Local credit refinement alone did not produce sustained access to compact, organized, functionalized chemistry. The result supports the implementation and shows a descriptive gain on this seed; it does not establish a reliable oracle-score benefit of selective credit. Larger changes in different objectives nearly cancel, some counted gains are near numerical ties, and the same-menu probability comparisons do not score unsubmitted alternatives. Whether broader molecular constraints or a better size and termination prior can make the now-demonstrated local discrimination useful remains open, as does its reliability across seeds.
finding_summary.results: The intended credit localization happened. Across the five task-specific tables, 3,027 attachment keys and 6,522 ring-closure keys separated previously shared neighborhoods. All 145 online winner updates withheld deposits from other neighborhoods when opportunities existed, totaling 75,964 alternative/update pairs. Every one of 10,719 mixed-neighborhood update probes increased the winner neighborhoods' conditional probability mass. Later construction contained 18,485 selected moves whose conditional probabilities changed and whose exact neighborhoods traced to earlier accepted online winners. The optimization gain was much smaller than the amount of activity. Among accepted ants that reused online credit, 7 of 1,396 beat their pre-batch incumbent, compared with 3 of 1,399 for the Parent; reuse still reached about 96% of accepted ants. All strict incumbent beaters increased from 8 to 12, but three of the new online-reusing docking beaters were steps of at most 0.00000044 along a low score plateau. The single screening seed's mean final Top-1 rose from 0.2523 to 0.2579. The sitagliptin multi-property score rose from 0.0980 to 0.2392, while dopamine-receptor docking fell from 0.1371 to 0.0289 and decoration hopping fell from 0.5534 to 0.5484. The zaleplon and median-molecule scores stayed at 0.3051 and 0.1678. No generated molecule beat the supplied starting incumbent on three of the five objectives. All 1,450 submitted molecules were accepted; one additional local construction repeated a molecule and was replaced before submission.

finding_summary.headline: Neighborhood credit localized and lifted the screening mean, but successful molecules remained rare
finding_summary.insights: This experiment separates local credit discrimination from productive molecular search. Different neighborhoods really were being collapsed by the old keys, and the new keys distinguish them without changing the legal chemistry or fixed heuristic weights. Matching neighborhoods also recur often enough to transfer credit across different partial molecules, so the refinement did not eliminate transfer through excessive sparsity. Yet most ants still inherit some online credit, and only 5.84% of the observed split-menu groups carried unequal refined pheromones. More precise keys therefore changed specific decisions without making successful whole molecules common. The chemistry explains why the modest mean gain should not be read as a broadly improved generator. The molecular assessment found a compact acyclic urea behind the strongest score increase, but long unsaturated chains and unconventional ring assemblies still dominate. Mean atom count fell slightly, while ring-closure actions fell sharply and terminations at the 64-atom ceiling became more frequent. In every task the late molecules were larger than the early molecules. Local credit refinement alone did not produce sustained access to compact, organized, functionalized chemistry. The result supports the implementation and shows a descriptive gain on this seed; it does not establish a reliable oracle-score benefit of selective credit. Larger changes in different objectives nearly cancel, some counted gains are near numerical ties, and the same-menu probability comparisons do not score unsubmitted alternatives. Whether broader molecular constraints or a better size and termination prior can make the now-demonstrated local discrimination useful remains open, as does its reliability across seeds.

molecular_assessment.headline: Long polyene chains dominate; occasional polar cages and a compact urea score better, but conventional scaffold chemistry remains sparse.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All five supplied task trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read for seed 0. Each contains 290 optimizer proposals plus 10 initial observations. The generated population consists mainly of long, repeatedly unsaturated carbon chains, interrupted by amines, enamines, occasional imines, ethers and carbonyls. Rings are substantial in amount but often unconventional in arrangement: partially unsaturated carbocycles and dense fused or bridged assemblies occur alongside isolated aryl segments. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.3966 to 0.8966, while aromatic-text rates range from 0.1241 to 0.5690; these are fractions of strings carrying a feature, not aromatic atom fractions or assessments of ring quality. Mean SMILES lengths range from 60.1 to 76.5. Direct atom counts from the trajectories show that shorter strings than the Parent frequently reflect fewer closures and branches rather than a substantial size reduction. The emitted structures have no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry, and inspection also found no specified alkene geometry. All supplied generated SMILES parsed with RDKit, which establishes readable molecular graphs, not stability or synthetic accessibility. The quality labels describe substantial ring occurrence, sparse aromatic organization, questionable preparative chemistry, weak resemblance to ordinary medicinal chemistry and recurrent polyene motifs despite distinct molecular identities. Atom and functional-group counts below are direct structural readings of the supplied SMILES; all scores are the recorded evaluator values. Digest medians displayed as 0.0 are rounded and must not be interpreted as a majority of exactly zero observations.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 73.6; direct heavy-atom counts average 47.46 and reach 64. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.8966 and 0.5690. Much of this ring content is a carbocycle or aryl segment embedded in a long polyene, rather than a compact aromatic scaffold. Evaluation 11, the best generated structure, is a compact, densely bridged nitrogen-containing polycycle bearing a nitrile, chlorine and cyclic ketones. Other higher examples include a partially unsaturated N/O polycycle and a nitrogen-free aryl-containing enone/aldehyde chain. Late structures are predominantly long hydrocarbon-rich polyenes, sometimes with ketones, aldehydes or a nitrile. Conventional fragments are recognizable, but their extended unsaturation and crowded ring combinations make synthesis and isolation questionable.
liabilities: Long polyenes and conjugated carbonyl chains create numerous unspecified alkene geometries and potential chemical-stability burdens.
Dense bridged rings with extensive unsaturation and unassigned stereochemistry need geometric and synthetic scrutiny; successful SMILES parsing does not resolve those concerns.
missing_features: Repeated production of compact, conventionally substituted aromatic NH heterocycles with an attached amide, as seen in the best supplied initial molecule; generated aromatic content is frequently carried on long unsaturated extensions.

Sustained access to the compact polar arrangements found among the higher generated examples. The final proposals mostly lose their concentrated nitrogen/carbonyl organization; the data do not identify one mandatory heteroatom motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 24-heavy-atom bridged nitrile at evaluation 11 scores 0.19324099086270913; the 21-heavy-atom N/O polycycle at evaluation 65 scores 0.17464941125558517. The nitrogen-free, shorter carbonyl-containing structure at evaluation 176 still scores 0.13915472870419515, so nitrogen alone cannot explain the gradient. Long final polyenes score zero or near zero; evaluation 300 has 64 heavy atoms and score 0.0. Exactly 130 of the 290 generated proposals score zero. The clearest association is with compactness and functional-group arrangement, not simply having a ring: many zero-scoring chains also contain rings. The supplied indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 remains best overall at 0.3051048083696145. Compared with Parent n-3ab6a944e3dd, ring-closure/aromatic-text rates rise from 0.6103/0.2172 to 0.8966/0.5690 and the generated maximum moves from 0.1775836262122333 to 0.19324099086270913, while that initial overall best remains unchanged.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 75.3 and direct heavy-atom count averages 50.05. Ring-closure rate is 0.8345, but aromatic-text rate is only 0.2655. The best generated molecule at evaluation 223 combines aryl-containing fused ring units, amide groups and nitrogen-containing linkers with a very long alkenyl appendage. Evaluation 26 is smaller and contains a fused N/O ring assembly, an amino substituent and an imine/N-N-containing chain. Other proposals distribute amines, enamines, imines, ethers and amides through long unsaturated backbones. The late molecules retain scattered rings and polar groups but look like extended polyene constructs; their synthesis is considerably less straightforward than the supplied conventionally substituted aromatic starting molecules.
liabilities: Extended polyenes with repeated amine/enamine and occasional imine or hydrazone-like functionality impose stability and stereochemical complexity.
Some highly fused N/O assemblies and densely unsaturated ring junctions have questionable preparative accessibility despite acceptable formal valence.
missing_features: Reliable production of clearly substituted aryl and carbonyl-bearing nitrogen heterocycle arrangements like those present in the stronger initial observations; such organization is diluted by unsaturated tails in much of the generated set.

approach.method_basis: The Parent is an ant colony optimizer that builds each molecular graph from an empty state. At each step it chooses a starting atom, attaches an atom to an existing site, closes a ring bond, or stops. Fixed aggregate frequencies from an unlabeled molecular corpus supply chemical preferences, including attachment, ring-closure and stopping weights. A separate table of task-local pheromones multiplies those preferences. The Parent identifies a reusable attachment component by the central atom's identity, charge, explicit hydrogens, degree, used bond order and ring membership, together with the proposed bond and new atom. Ring-closure components use both endpoint descriptions and their path length. Initial reinforcement comes from an exact reconstruction of the best supported starting observation. After feedback, all pheromones evaporate and only the highest-scoring accepted molecule in that batch deposits credit on its actual construction trace, once per distinct key. Positive lower and upper bounds preserve exploration. Later ants share the credited local components even when they occur inside different partial molecules.
approach.novelty: I add neighborhood-resolved pheromone credit: an attachment site also carries a sorted description of its directly bonded neighbors, and a ring closure carries this description at both endpoints. A move that was rewarded beside one arrangement of atoms and bonds will therefore share that reward only with the same bounded neighborhood. For example, the same central carbon description can acquire different credit when its neighboring atom is oxygen instead of carbon. This tests the Parent's observed loss of selectivity, where almost every accepted ant reused reinforcement but very few improved the incumbent. The lineage currently contains only the original ant colony root, so no sibling has tested a finer pheromone key. The corpus-derived heuristic still uses its original contexts; the new distinction acts specifically through which construction decisions share accepted winner credit.
